retainedReference.title: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
retainedReference.description: temple of Shivan (Kapaleeswarar) and a form of Shiva's consort Parvati called Karpagambal ("Goddess of the Wish-Yielding Tree"), located in Mylapore, Chennai in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu
retainedReference.reason: No unique physical footprint or centerline with exact Wikidata identity has been resolved.

pictures.author: KurinchiRays
pictures.observations: Entire500x667 current color photograph inspected. Seven receding tiers with dense polychrome figures, blue-green/pink/cream trim, grey dressed granite gateway base/pilasters, broad curved crest and finials. Model uses original simplified ornament, not copied deity inventory.

pictures.author: Roehan Rengadurai
pictures.observations: Entire960x539 monochrome upward front detail inspected. Repeating stepped cornices, central stacked dark niches, miniature crowned figures and arched/scroll shrine surrounds. Monochrome picture is a geometry reference, not a color reference.

pictures.author: Sailko
pictures.observations: Entire960x643 ordinary courtyard picture inspected. Open flat-roofed stone mandapa with several square piers and real gaps, layered cornice, narrow red/white roof trim, small painted roof sculptures and tall brass flagstaff. Exact inner shrine roof hidden by hall.

pictures.author: H. Grobe
pictures.date: 2012 upload/scan metadata; historical picture date unresolved
pictures.observations: Entire960x621 historical-looking courtyard scan inspected. Open pillared hall fronts, red/white parapet rhythm and several shrine/gateway masses. Used only as supplementary spatial/colonnade reference; current tower palette comes from the2025 color photograph, and horizontal positions from standard PMTiles.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Specific Kapaleeshwarar standing core: twelve mapped gateway/shrine/mandapa/perimeter-roof envelopes, tall seven-tier eastern gopuram and smaller western gopuram with true through-passages, granite bases and receding painted bands/central niches, curved crests/finials and original simplified sculptural vocabulary. Two inner shrine roof masses, real open pillared mandapas, red/white parapet rhythms, stone plinths and brass flagstaff. Courtyards, tank, streets and independent surrounding buildings stay host context. No copied deity/narrative/text atlas or complete ritual interior.
